standard.title: Aesthetic qualities of authorial style
standard.description: analyse texts and evaluate the aesthetic qualities and appeal of an author's literary style
standard.prior_knowledge: Students discuss the aesthetic and social value of literary texts using appropriate metalanguage (AC9E7LE04). They have not yet analysed and evaluated the aesthetic qualities of a specific author's literary style as a distinctive and comparably assessed set of choices.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse and evaluate the aesthetic qualities and appeal of an author's literary style.

nodes.label: Identifying authorial style
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify features of an author's literary style — the consistent patterns of language, structure and technique that characterise their writing.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three consistent stylistic features across two or more texts by the same author, explaining what each feature contributes to the author's style.
nodes.typical_width: Compare texts created by the same author to determine literary style — examining vocabulary patterns, sentence structure, narrative techniques, and thematic concerns as consistent stylistic markers.
wider: Investigate how an author's style changed over their career, and evaluate what drove the evolution
Compare an author's fiction style with their non-fiction (where available) and examine what remains consistent

response_modes.reason: Identifying style requires students to have accumulated enough features from enough texts to recognise patterns rather than isolated choices. Two texts minimum; three is better. Building a catalogue of features before evaluating is necessary.

success_criteria: Student identifies at least two consistent stylistic features across multiple texts
Student names specific textual evidence for each stylistic feature identified
nodes.hinge_reason: Evaluating aesthetic quality (N2) requires a catalogue of identified stylistic features to evaluate — students who haven't built that catalogue from multiple texts have no raw material to assess at N2.

nodes.label: Evaluating aesthetic qualities and appeal
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate the aesthetic qualities of an author's literary style — making and supporting judgements about what makes the style effective, distinctive or appealing.
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate the aesthetic appeal of one aspect of an author's style, explaining what makes it effective and how it contributes to the overall literary experience.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse and evaluate the aesthetic qualities of an author's literary style — assessing its appeal, explaining its distinctiveness, and presenting comparisons to others.
wider: Present a comparison of two authors' styles, evaluating the relative aesthetic appeal of each and arguing for a judgement about which is more effective for a particular literary purpose
Examine how cultural background and context shape what readers find aesthetically appealing in literary style — analysing where aesthetic preferences are culturally situated

response_modes.reason: Evaluating aesthetic quality requires students to move from 'I find this appealing' to 'this has aesthetic quality because...' — a reasoning move from subjective response to grounded evaluation. The criteria for aesthetic judgement need explicit scaffolding to produce substantiated evaluation rather than preference assertion.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Literary style evaluation is the core of advanced literary appreciation and directly motivates students' own writing development. The elaboration explicitly includes 'presenting comparisons to others' — the sharing of aesthetic evaluation as a social literary practice is rich pedagogical territory.
success_criteria: Student makes a specific evaluative claim about the author's style (not just description)
Student supports the evaluation with at least two pieces of textual evidence
